**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize required builds on the Coolify host**

For a non-doc PR this job runs the full suite including `npm run build` on the Coolify self-hosted pool, while `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` now targets the same pool and its Playwright webServer runs `npm run build && npm run start`. The rollout note documents two Linux runners on the same Hetzner/Coolify box, so GitHub can schedule these builds concurrently and across PRs, outside Coolify's `concurrent_builds=1` throttle; AGENTS.md calls out parallel builds as the OOM/disk failure mode on this production host. Add a shared concurrency group, use a single CI runner label, or otherwise ensure only one Next build hits the box at a time.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 16492118. All rerouted jobs now target the single dedicated `[self-hosted, socratic-ci]` runner label, so GitHub serializes the full builds and the `socratic-deploy` lane remains reserved. The Coolify runner service was also restarted after both Socratic containers exited.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add a same-repo gate before Codex autofix hits self-hosted**

When Codex reviews a fork or otherwise untrusted PR, this `pull_request_review` workflow can now be assigned to the persistent Coolify runner, and GitHub's event ref is the PR merge branch; the job then checks it out and launches a Bash-capable Claude action with whatever write tokens/secrets are available. The CI/e2e/security jobs added source-refusal checks for this self-hosted migration, but this PR-triggered autofix job did not, so add a job-level `head.repo.full_name == github.repository`/trusted-actor guard or keep this workflow on hosted runners.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 049d8475. The autofix job now has a job-level same-repository admission check for `pull_request_review` events (`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`) in addition to the Codex-bot check. Fork PRs therefore never reach the persistent runner, checkout, write token, or model secret; maintainer `workflow_dispatch` remains available.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run CI failure reporting outside socratic-ci**

When the `socratic-ci` runner is the component that disappears or becomes unhealthy, this `workflow_run` reporter is queued on that same label, so the Sentry failure event / cron check-in for the failed CI, smoke, or security workflow cannot be emitted until the runner has already recovered (and may never emit if the queued self-hosted job expires). I inspected the rerouted CI/e2e/security workflows in this change and they also depend on `[self-hosted, socratic-ci]`; keep this reporter on an independent runner/hosted fallback so runner outages are still observable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 6b99b9a5. The failure/schedule-only reporter now runs on the separate `[self-hosted, socratic-deploy]` runner, so a missing or unhealthy `socratic-ci` registration cannot suppress its Sentry event. GitHub-hosted admission is the outage this PR is recovering from, so the independent Coolify runner is the available fallback; it also has the bounded per-registration `/_work` cleanup.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Set up Node for the migrated pin check**

After this job moves off `ubuntu-latest`, the script still invokes `node` directly (`LOCAL_SPEC`, `parse_ref_json`, and `PEER_SPEC`) without an `actions/setup-node` step. On a clean `socratic-ci` runner where Node is not already on PATH, the weekly/PR shared-package drift check fails before it can compare pins; add the same Node setup used by the other migrated Node workflows before running this shell script.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Verified without a workflow change. The first clean-runner execution, run 29643331337, completed this job successfully, including every direct `node` invocation in the comparison script. The pinned `myoung34/github-runner:2.335.1-ubuntu-noble` image installs `nodejs` in its base image, so an additional setup/download step would be redundant.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Install gh and jq before running merge shepherd**

Moving the shepherd off `ubuntu-latest` also removes the hosted image's guaranteed GitHub CLI/jq toolchain, but `scripts/merge-shepherd.sh` calls `gh pr list` before it can scan anything and then uses `jq` for every PR. On a bare Coolify runner image without those commands on PATH, manual shepherd dispatches fail immediately and leave auto-merge-armed PRs stuck; install the tools in this job or keep this automation on an image that provides them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Verified against the pinned runner image rather than adding redundant per-job apt work. `myoung34/github-runner:2.335.1-ubuntu-noble` installs `jq` as an essential and `github-cli` through its base-image config; the same live runner also completed the GitHub-API-based shared-pin check in run 29643331337. The shepherd retains its existing `gh`/`jq` implementation.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore full history for gitleaks scans**

In `pull_request` and scheduled security runs, this shallow checkout gives gitleaks only the triggering merge/head commit, so a secret that was added and then removed in an earlier PR commit, or exists only in older history, is no longer available to the scan. This regresses the workflow's stated goal of scanning every diff, and the gitleaks-action usage example also checks out full history (`fetch-depth: 0`), so keep the full history or explicitly fetch the PR commit range before invoking gitleaks: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks-action#usage-example

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in e694ac70. Security is restored to `fetch-depth: 0`; the shallow/tag-free/event-SHA optimization now applies only to the lightweight classifier jobs. Gitleaks therefore retains visibility into secrets added and removed in earlier PR commits and scheduled repository history.
